title: arXiv AI — latest announcement batch 2026-11-19: 10 papers on embodied reasoning, video understanding, and visual-model design
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This inferred ordering prioritizes deterministic, checkable attention signals; citation evidence is sparse for these recent papers, and the list is not a most-read or most-downloaded ranking.

sections.title: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation
sections.abstract: The authors introduce a 30-task simulated manipulation benchmark that separately probes history-based reasoning, precise action, and closed-loop composition, finding that even their strongest evaluated agent succeeds on only 12.0% of Mind2Act episodes.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors provide 180 task configurations across three views and a diagnosis harness; their evaluation reports a large gap between Mind/Act performance (52.7%/39.0% for the strongest agent) and Mind2Act performance (12.0%).
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say the views are different tasks, not matched interventions, so longer horizons and early execution errors cannot yet be separated from a composition deficit; all tasks are simulated tabletop manipulation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Highest collected score 13.953: 49 Hugging Face paper upvotes, 30 GitHub stars, and two cross-lists; weighted components are HF 11.736, code stars 1.717, cross-lists 0.500.

sections.title: WeMM-Video: Pushing the Frontiers of Open-Source Omni-Modal Video Understanding
sections.abstract: The authors present Chinese-English 2B–35B-A3B models that jointly process text, image, audio, and video with fast-instruct and reasoning modes, reporting evaluations across more than 120 benchmarks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that WeMM-Video-35B-A3B leads their open-source comparisons on omni-modal video tasks and that the 9B variant outperforms the compared 30B open-source model; they release weights and an evaluation/reproduction pipeline.
sections.unique_caveat: For existing comparison models, the paper uses official scores where available and its own evaluations otherwise, so not every comparison is from a single uniform evaluation run.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collected score 13.675: 43 Hugging Face paper upvotes, 62 GitHub stars, one cross-list; weighted components are HF 11.353, code stars 2.072, cross-lists 0.250.

sections.title: Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth
sections.abstract: The authors present a native-resolution network for metric depth from images and video, designed to combine sharp boundaries with temporal consistency and reporting a new Pareto frontier across accuracy, sharpness, consistency, and runtime.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper describes a shared multi-frame transformer, multi-view consistency training, and a family of models; its abstract reports improvements over prior work in metric accuracy, boundary sharpness, and temporal consistency.
sections.unique_caveat: The multi-view consistency loss uses ground-truth camera poses and ground-truth depth to exclude occluded or moving pixels during training, a supervision requirement relevant to reproducing that objective.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collected score 13.280: 29 Hugging Face paper upvotes, 284 GitHub stars, one cross-list; weighted components are HF 10.204, code stars 2.826, cross-lists 0.250.

sections.title: Coda-DaVinci: Reimagining Video Generation with Code2Video
sections.abstract: The authors study agent-authored 3D proxies for video generation and introduce a task-adaptive framework that selects direct or proxy-guided generation, with proxy granularity, simulation, and prompting evaluated through controlled experiments and blinded human ratings.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that coarse proxies favor natural motion while medium-grained proxies favor consistency, and that their framework improves instruction following, scene consistency, physical plausibility, and visual realism on the evaluated comparisons.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract reports remaining long-video weaknesses in transition stability and adherence to scene settings.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collected score 12.319: 35 Hugging Face paper upvotes and 22 GitHub stars; weighted components are HF 10.751 and code stars 1.568.

sections.title: Posterior Matching Distillation
sections.abstract: The authors propose Posterior Matching Distillation, which matches reweighted student-sample means to teacher posterior means to preserve the teacher’s image distribution while allowing stochastic generation at any trained timestep budget.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors prove a posterior-identification result under their stated conditions and report the best FID among evaluated four-step methods on SDXL and FLUX.2 [klein], with competitive prompt-alignment and perceptual scores.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported empirical comparison is limited to SDXL and FLUX.2 [klein] and the evaluated four-step setting; broader model and sampling-budget behavior is not established by those results.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collected score 12.115: 36 Hugging Face paper upvotes and 12 GitHub stars; weighted components are HF 10.833 and code stars 1.282.

sections.title: Probing the "Conscious" Mind: Selective Access and Global Workspace in Vision-Language Models
sections.abstract: The authors introduce a multimodal Jacobian lens that maps vision and language representations to a shared output-vocabulary semantic space and use interventions to study selective concept access and downstream effects in vision-language models.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper reports that concepts are readable and selectively accessible in intermediate states, that counterfactual interventions affect downstream computation, and that its J-space metrics track cross-modal alignment across tested VLM families and sizes.
sections.unique_caveat: These are probe- and intervention-based findings in tested VLMs; they do not establish that the models are conscious, and conclusions depend on the lens’s decoder-vocabulary readout.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collected score 11.784: 42 Hugging Face paper upvotes and two cross-lists; weighted components are HF 11.284 and cross-lists 0.500, with no code-star component recorded.

sections.title: HiUni: Harmonizing Understanding and Generation in Shared Visual Space
sections.abstract: The authors extend a pretrained vision-language model with a shared language-aligned ViT and dense Transformer backbone for understanding and image generation, adding a Pixel Diffusion Head and HiGate pathway for synthesis and spatial detail.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report an average understanding score similar to the pretrained VLM alongside competitive image generation and editing, and argue that one dense backbone can support both without task-specific backbone computation.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract characterizes generation and editing as competitive rather than claiming uniform state-of-the-art performance; the evidence is limited to the reported tasks and comparisons.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collected score 11.138: 23 Hugging Face paper upvotes, 14 GitHub stars, one cross-list; weighted components are HF 9.534, code stars 1.354, cross-lists 0.250.

sections.title: ZeroVLN: Learning to Navigate without Supervised Fine-Tuning of the VLM Brain
sections.abstract: The authors propose a slow-fast vision-language navigation framework that leaves the VLM brain without navigation-domain supervised fine-tuning, instead using natural-language tool calls to an adapted action expert and closed-loop reinforcement learning.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that ZeroVLN outperforms the compared SFT-based hierarchical methods on VLN-CE benchmarks while making only minor changes to the VLM brain and largely preserving its general visual capabilities.
sections.unique_caveat: “Zero SFT” applies to the VLM brain: the action expert is adapted and both policies are improved through RL on navigation episodes; the reported evaluation is on benchmarks, not a real-world deployment.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collected score 10.952: 22 Hugging Face paper upvotes and 21 GitHub stars; weighted components are HF 9.406 and code stars 1.546.

sections.title: EgoCaptioner: Towards Comprehensive and Fine-Grained Egocentric Video Captioning
sections.abstract: The authors combine video-level context with timestamped egocentric action descriptions, using 50,000 coarse-to-fine training examples and factual, coverage, and temporal-alignment rewards to refine captions.
sections.claimed_contribution: Across five egocentric benchmarks, the authors report leading results among evaluated open-source models for caption quality, caption-conditioned QA, and temporal alignment, with ablations supporting multiple reward terms and coarse-to-fine annotations.
sections.unique_caveat: Pose-derived motion facts are used only where sensor data are available, so that additional factual-supervision path is not present for every source video.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collected score 10.747: 25 Hugging Face paper upvotes and six GitHub stars; weighted components are HF 9.774 and code stars 0.973.

sections.title: TuringSpace: Grounding Spatial Intelligence in Action with Interactive CAPTCHAs
sections.abstract: The authors introduce 125 programmatically generated interactive CAPTCHA tasks for spatial action, report a 25.9% failure rate for their best tested model, and show that fine-tuning Qwen3.5-9B on the environment raises success from 1.6% to 33.1%.
sections.claimed_contribution: The benchmark tests five spatial abilities through clicks and drags, provides generated instances with checkers and oracles, and the authors report gains on seven out-of-distribution benchmarks after fine-tuning.
sections.unique_caveat: The central task set is a synthetic CAPTCHA environment; transfer to seven external benchmarks is encouraging but does not by itself establish reliability across open-ended real-world spatial interaction.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collected score 10.339: 23 Hugging Face paper upvotes and four GitHub stars; weighted components are HF 9.534 and code stars 0.805.
